issue: Can a state-law controlled substance offense serve as a predicate under U.S.S.G. § 2K2.1(a)(4)(A) when the state's definition of a controlled substance is broader than the federal Controlled Substances Act's?

sides.position: Courts may consider state-law controlled substance offenses under § 2K2.1(a)(4)(A) even if the state defines a controlled substance differently from the federal CSA, based on the Guidelines' textual inclusion of state-law offenses.
cases: United States v. Jones, 81 F.4th 591 (6th Cir. 2023)

sides.position: A state-law controlled substance offense must be measured against the federal definition of a controlled substance (federal-law-only approach), which the opinion says Jones advanced for uniformity. The excerpts do not identify which circuits hold this position.

this_court: Sixth Circuit takes the side that courts may consider state-law controlled substance offenses under § 2K2.1(a)(4)(A), rejecting the federal-law-only approach.
quote: Today, we take one side of a circuit split. Using a textual analysis, the Third, Fourth, Seventh, Eighth, and Tenth Circuits have held that courts may consider state-law controlled substance offenses under § 2K2.1(a)(4)(A).
cite: United States v. T'Shaun Omar Jones, 81 F.4th 591 (6th Cir. 2023)
